newsitem.title: USA: Envirodyne says deal worth about $652 mln.
newsitem.headline: Envirodyne says deal worth about $652 mln.

text.p: Envirodyne Industries Inc said Thursday a proposed acquisition offer from HK Acquisitions Corp would include about $127 million in cash for equity and the assumption of $525 million of debt, for a total value of $652 million.
Earlier, Envirodyne said it received an offer from HK to purchase the outstanding shares of the company for $8.50 a shares.
HK was formed by Michael Heisley, a current Envirodyne director, and Donald Kelly, former Envirodyne chairman. Kelly is not a current Envirodyne board member, a spokesman said.
Envirodyne said the offer was contained in a proposed letter agreement requiring a response from the company by the close of business on June 18.
The proposal also calls for a $10 million fee to be paid to HK in the event that Envirodyne agreed to the deal and then terminated it in favor of another acquisition offer.
A company spokesman said Envirodyne has no other pending acquisition offers. The HK offer will be evaluated by a panel of independent directors.
In May, Zapata Corp said it terminated its $8 a share proposal to acquire all the common stock of Envirodyne that it did not already own.
